questions.text: What was Friday called before the advent of Islam?
questions.explanation: Before the advent of Islam, Friday was called Yawm al-Arubah by the Arabs. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, arabia before islam (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who among the following was a direct ancestor of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is a direct descendant of Hazrat Ismaeel (AS) through the lineage of Adnan and the Arabized Arabs (Mustariba). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, arabia before islam.

questions.text: What is the period between the time of Prophet Jesus (Hazrat Essa) and the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) known as?
questions.explanation: The period between Prophet Jesus (Hazrat Essa علیہ السلام) and Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is known as the Period of Fatrah (Fitrah). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, arabia before islam.

questions.text: What were the alternative names for the city of Makkah during the pre-Islamic period?
questions.explanation: During the pre-Islamic period, Makkah was known by several alternative names including Bakkah, Umm al-Qura, and Al-Balad al-Amin. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, arabia before islam.

questions.text: What term is used to describe the era before the advent of Islam in Arabia?
questions.explanation: The era before the advent of Islam in Arabia is called the Age of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, arabia before islam.

questions.text: What was the name of the most revered goddess among the Quraish tribe before the advent of Islam?
questions.explanation: The most revered goddess among the Quraish tribe before Islam was Al-Uzza. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, arabia before islam.

questions.text: Who was the childhood friend of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The childhood friend of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, birth early life (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: For how many years did Hazrat Abd-al-Muttalib care for the Holy Prophet before his own death?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Abd-al-Muttalib cared for the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for two years before his own death. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, birth early life.

questions.text: Where did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) undertake his first business journey?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) undertook his first business journey to Syria at the age of 12, accompanying his uncle Abu Talib. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, birth early life.

questions.text: What was the birth year of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) famously known as?
questions.explanation: The birth year of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is famously known as the Year of Elephant (Aam-ul-Feel). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, birth early life.

questions.text: Who was the mother of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W)?
questions.explanation: The mother of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) was Hazrat Amina (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, birth early life.

questions.text: In which year did the marriage of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadijah (R.A) take place?
questions.explanation: The marriage of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadijah (R.A) took place in 595 A.D. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, birth early life.

questions.text: During the formation of the Brotherhood Pact in Yathrib, how many Muhajreen were there?
questions.explanation: Low confidence: Mawakhat paired about 45 Muhajireen with 45 Ansar (90 people), per Ibn Sa'd. At the time of the Brotherhood Pact (Muwakhat) in Yathrib, there were 45 Muhajreen. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: Who were the Ansar in the context of the brotherhood pact?
questions.explanation: The Ansar were the Muslims from Madina who welcomed and supported the Muhajirun (migrants from Makkah) under the brotherhood pact established by the Prophet (PBUH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: Who were the two groups between whom the bond of 'Muwakhaat' was established by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The bond of 'Muwakhaat' (brotherhood) was established by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) between the Ansaar and Muhaajireen. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: Who were the Ashaab-e-Suffah in Islamic history?

options.A: Ansar (RA) who hosted the Muhajirs in Madina
options.B: Muhajirs (RA) who stayed near the Masjid-e-Nabvi
options.C: Sahaba (RA) who compiled the Quran during the Prophet's life
options.D: Companions (RA) who fought in the Battle of Badr

questions.explanation: The Ashaab-e-Suffah were the Muhajirs (RA) who stayed near the Masjid-e-Nabvi on a raised platform (Suffah) dedicated to learning and worship. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: What does the term 'Akhuwwat' refer to in Islamic teachings?
questions.explanation: The term 'Akhuwwat' in Islamic teachings refers to Brotherhood. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: During the Brotherhood Pact in Madina, at whose house did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) gather the Muhajireen and Ansar?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) gathered the Muhajireen and Ansar for the Brotherhood Pact at the house of Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: How many months after the migration to Madinah was the Brotherhood Pact (Mawakhat) established?
questions.explanation: Low confidence: the time after Hijrah given for Mawakhat varies by source (about 5–8 months). The Brotherhood Pact (Mawakhat) between the Muhajireen and Ansar was established five months after the migration to Madinah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: How many Arab tribes were present in Madina at the time of the brotherhood pact?
questions.explanation: At the time of the brotherhood pact (Muwakhat), there were two main Arab tribes in Madina: the Aws and the Khazraj. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, brotherhood.

questions.text: In which Surah of the Quran is the change of Qiblah mentioned?
questions.explanation: The change of Qiblah is mentioned in Surah Baqarah (Chapter 2 of the Holy Quran). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, change of qibla.

questions.text: What significant event took place at Masjid al-Qiblatayn regarding the direction of prayer?

options.A: Changed Qiblah from Jerusalem to Makkah
options.B: Changed Qiblah from Makkah to Jerusalem
options.D: First congregational Eid prayer was held

questions.explanation: At Masjid al-Qiblatayn, the Qiblah was changed from Jerusalem to Makkah during a congregational prayer. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, change of qibla.

questions.text: In which Hijri year was the Qibla changed from Jerusalem to Kaaba?
questions.explanation: The Qibla was changed from Jerusalem to the Kaaba in 2 AH. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, change of qibla (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What is considered the first written constitution in the world?
questions.explanation: The first written constitution in the world is Meesaq-e-Madina (the Charter of Medina). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, charter of madina (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who were the signatories of the Constitution of Madina?

options.C: Muslims (Muhajireen and Ansar) and non-Muslim tribes

questions.explanation: The Constitution of Madina was signed by Muslims (Muhajireen and Ansar) and non-Muslim tribes, establishing the first pluralistic Islamic state. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, charter of madina.

questions.text: The Charter of Medina was concluded between which groups?

options.D: Muslims and the Quraysh of Makkah

questions.explanation: The Charter of Medina was concluded between Muslims, Jews, and other non-Muslims residing in Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, charter of madina.

questions.text: In which year was the Charter (Meesaq) of Madina signed?
questions.explanation: The Charter (Meesaq) of Madina was signed in 1 A.H. / 622 A.D., shortly after the Prophet's (PBUH) migration to Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, charter of madina.

questions.text: Who is credited with describing the Charter of Madina as the world's first written constitution?
questions.explanation: The Charter of Madina is described as the world's first written constitution by Muhammad Hamidullah, a renowned Islamic scholar and jurist. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, charter of madina.

questions.text: Which Jewish tribe in Madinah was led by the chieftain Huyayy ibn Akhtab?
questions.explanation: The Jewish tribe led by Huyayy ibn Akhtab in Madinah was Banu Nadir. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, charter of madina.

questions.text: Who was entrusted with the keys to the Kaaba at the time of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The keys to the Kaaba were entrusted to Hazrat Usman bin Talha (RA) at the time of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, conquest of makkah.

questions.text: What phrase did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) recite while removing idols from the Kaaba?

options.A: Victory belongs to Allah, the Lord of the worlds
options.B: There is no god but Allah alone
options.C: Allah is the Greatest, and all praise belongs to Him
options.D: Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished

questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) recited "Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished" while removing idols from the Kaaba. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, conquest of makkah.

questions.text: During the advance towards Makkah for the conquest, where was the Prophet's (PBUH) final encampment?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) made his final encampment at Mura Zahran during the advance towards the conquest of Makkah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, conquest of makkah.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the governor of Makkah by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the Conquest of Makkah?
questions.explanation: After the Conquest of Makkah, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Attab Bin Usaid (R.A) as the governor of Makkah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, conquest of makkah.

questions.text: How many companions accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the conquest of Makkah?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was accompanied by 10,000 companions during the conquest of Makkah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, conquest of makkah.

questions.text: Which places were declared safe for those who sought refuge during the Conquest of Makkah?

options.C: Their own homes with doors locked

questions.explanation: During the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet (PBUH) declared that those who entered the house of Abu Sufyan, the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), or their own homes with doors locked would be safe. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, conquest of makkah.

questions.text: How many years did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions endure the siege in Shi'ab-e-Abi-Talib?
questions.explanation: The siege of Shi'ab-e-Abi-Talib lasted for 3 years, from the 7th to the 10th year of Prophethood. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: For how many years did the social boycott of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by the Quraysh last?
questions.explanation: The social boycott of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by the Quraysh lasted for 3 years. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: Where is Masjid al-Jinn located?
questions.explanation: Masjid al-Jinn is located in Makkah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: Abu Jahl, a prominent opponent of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), was the chief of which tribe?
questions.explanation: Abu Jahl, one of the fiercest opponents of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), was the chief of Banu Makhzum. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: During which event did Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ait place the camel's intestines on the Holy Prophet's back while he was in prostration?
questions.explanation: Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ait placed camel intestines on the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) back during a prayer in Makkah while he was in prostration. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: During which event was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) subjected to a social boycott by the Quraysh?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was subjected to a social boycott by the Quraysh during the Shoib Abi Talib (Valley of Abu Talib). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: Where did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) establish the first Islamic learning center known as Dar-e-Arqam?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) established the first Islamic learning center, Dar-e-Arqam, in Makkah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, early preaching persecution.

questions.text: Which speech is known as the first Charter of Human Rights in Islamic history?

options.A: Sermon of the Conquest of Makkah

questions.explanation: The Khutba-Hajjat-ul-Vida (Farewell Sermon) delivered by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during his last Hajj is recognized as the first Charter of Human Rights in Islamic history. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, farewell sermon (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: On which hill did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) deliver the Khutba of Hajjat ul Wida?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) delivered the Khutba of Hajjat ul Wida on Jabal al-Rehmat (the Mount of Mercy) at Arafat. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, farewell sermon.

questions.text: Before his passing, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) advised kind treatment towards which group?
questions.explanation: Fixed: in his final illness the Prophet (PBUH) urged the Muhajireen to treat the Ansar kindly (Sahih al-Bukhari, Manaqib al-Ansar). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, farewell sermon.

questions.text: In which year did the Holy Prophet (SAW) perform his farewell pilgrimage, known as Hajjat-ul-Wada?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet (SAW) performed his farewell pilgrimage, Hajjat-ul-Wada, in 10th Hijri. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, farewell sermon.

questions.text: On what date did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) pass away?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) passed away on 8th June 632 AD, corresponding to 12th Rabi-ul-Awwal 11 AH. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, farewell sermon.

questions.text: At what age did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) pass away?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) passed away at the age of 63 years. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, farewell sermon.

questions.text: The Battle of Badr was fought in which Islamic month?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr was fought in the Islamic month of Ramazan. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa badr (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which battle is known as Yaumul Furqan in Islamic history?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr is known as Yaumul Furqan (the Day of Criterion) because it was the first decisive battle that distinguished truth from falsehood in Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa badr (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: When was the Battle of Badr fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr was fought on 13 March 624 CE (17 Ramadan 2 AH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa badr (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who was the first to raise the flag in a Ghazwa for the Muslims?
questions.explanation: Low confidence: Hazrat Hamza (RA) carried the first banner, on the Sif al-Bahr expedition (1 AH). Some sources say Ubaidah bin Harith (RA). The first to raise the flag in a Ghazwa for the Muslims was Hazrat Hamza (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa badr (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: How many members of the Quraysh tribe were captured by the Muslims during the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: The Muslims captured 70 members of the Quraysh tribe during the Battle of Badr. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa badr.

questions.text: How many Muslims were martyred in the Ghazwa Badar?
questions.explanation: In the Ghazwa Badar, 14 Muslims were martyred. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa badr.

questions.text: In which Hijri year did the Battle of Hunain take place?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Hunain took place in 8th Hijri. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa hunain.

questions.text: On 1st Shawwal, 8th Hijra, how many soldiers were in the strong Islamic force that approached the valley of Hunain?
questions.explanation: The strong Islamic force that approached the valley of Hunain on 1st Shawwal, 8th Hijra, consisted of 12,000 soldiers. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa hunain.

questions.text: Who was the leader of the Banu Hawazin during the Battle of Hunain?
questions.explanation: The leader of the Banu Hawazin during the Battle of Hunain was Malik ibn Auf. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa hunain.

questions.text: Who was sent by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to encircle the Valley of Autas during the Battle of Hunain?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent Abu Amir Ashari (R.A) to encircle the Valley of Autas during the Battle of Hunain. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa hunain.

questions.text: Which Ghazwa was fought immediately after the Fatah Makkah?
questions.explanation: The Ghazwa fought immediately after Fatah Makkah was Ghazwa Hunain. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa hunain.

questions.text: Who were the adversaries of the Prophet (PBUH) and his companions in the Battle of Hunain?
questions.explanation: The adversaries of the Prophet (PBUH) and his companions in the Battle of Hunain were Hawazin and Thaqif. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa hunain.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the arbitrator in the matter of Banu Qurayza?
questions.explanation: The arbitrator appointed in the matter of Banu Qurayza was Hazrat Sa'ad bin Mu'adh (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khandaq (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who was the Muslim warrior that killed the pagan Amr ibn Abd al-Wud during the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwa Khandaq)?
questions.explanation: The Muslim warrior who killed the pagan champion Amr ibn Abd al-Wud during the Battle of the Trench was Hazrat Ali (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khandaq (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who suggested digging a trench as a defensive strategy in the Battle of the Trench?
questions.explanation: The strategy of digging a trench in the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwa Khandaq) was suggested by Hazrat Salman Farsi (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khandaq.

questions.text: During the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwa Khandaq), which tribe inside Madinah betrayed the Muslims?
questions.explanation: During the Battle of the Trench, the Jewish tribe Banu Qurayza betrayed the Muslims by siding with the Quraysh-led confederates. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khandaq.

questions.text: In which battle did Allah send cold, strong winds to aid the Muslims against their enemies?
questions.explanation: Allah sent cold, strong winds to aid the Muslims during Ghazwa Khandaq (the Battle of the Trench). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khandaq.

questions.text: Which battle occurred immediately before the Ghazwa Banu Qurayzah?
questions.explanation: The battle that occurred immediately before Ghazwa Banu Qurayzah was Ghazwa Khandaq (Trench). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khandaq.

questions.text: What was the main Jewish settlement about a hundred miles from Madina on the route to Syria, consisting of a series of forts?
questions.explanation: The main Jewish settlement about a hundred miles from Madina on the route to Syria, consisting of a series of forts, was Khyber. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khyber.

questions.text: Which group held the stronghold of Khyber during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The stronghold of Khyber during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was held by the Jews. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khyber.

questions.text: In which battle was Marhab killed during the Prophet's time?
questions.explanation: Marhab, the famous Jewish warrior, was killed during the Battle of Khaibar in 7 AH. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khyber.

questions.text: During which significant event was the Holy Prophet ﷺ poisoned by a lady named Zainab?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet ﷺ was poisoned by a Jewish lady named Zainab bint Al-Harith during the Conquest of Khyber. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khyber.

questions.text: Who among the companions ate the poisoned food along with the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of Ghazwa Khyber?
questions.explanation: The companion who ate the poisoned food along with the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at Ghazwa Khyber and was martyred due to it was Hazrat Bashr bin Bara (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khyber.

questions.text: What was the name of the main fort of the Jews at Khybar, considered invincible?
questions.explanation: The main fort of the Jews at Khybar, considered invincible, was Qamoos. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa khyber.

questions.text: In which battle was Hazrat Jaffar Tayyar martyred?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Jaffar Tayyar (R.A) was martyred in the Battle of Moota (8 AH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa mauta (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who was appointed as the leader of the Muslim army after the martyrdom of Hazrat Zaid Bin Haritha in the Battle of Muta?
questions.explanation: After the martyrdom of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (R.A) in the Battle of Muta, the leadership was assumed by Hazrat Jafar ibn Abi Talib (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa mauta.

questions.text: Who took over the command of the Muslim army after Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) in the Battle of Mota?
questions.explanation: After the martyrdom of Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) in the Battle of Mota, the command was taken over by Hazrat Abdullah bin Rawaha (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa mauta.

questions.text: During the Battle of Mauta, how many swords did Khalid Bin Walid (RA) break?
questions.explanation: During the Battle of Mauta, Khalid Bin Walid (RA) broke nine swords while fighting valiantly. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa mauta.

questions.text: How many Muslim soldiers were martyred in the Battle of Mauta?
questions.explanation: Note: most Seerah sources say 12 Muslims were martyred at Mu'tah. In the Battle of Mauta, 12 Muslim soldiers were martyred. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa mauta.

questions.text: During the Ghazwa Tabuk, what punishment was given to the famous Companions who stayed behind?
questions.explanation: The punishment given to the famous Companions who stayed behind during Ghazwa Tabuk was Social Boycott. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa tabuk.

questions.text: During which Ghazwa did Hazrat Uthman (R.A) donate nine hundred camels, one hundred horses, and ten thousand dinars?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Uthman (R.A) donated nine hundred camels, one hundred horses, and ten thousand dinars during Ghazwa Tabuk. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa tabuk.

questions.text: During which Ghazwa was Hazrat Ali (R.A) appointed as the caretaker of Madina by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Ali (R.A) was appointed as the caretaker of Madina by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) during Ghazwa Tabuk. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa tabuk.

questions.text: During which expedition in 9th Hijri did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) lead a 30,000 strong force to the border of Syria?
questions.explanation: In the 9th Hijri, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) led a 30,000-strong army to the border of Syria during the Expedition of Tabuk. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa tabuk.

questions.text: In which Ghazwa did the hypocrites make an excuse of extreme weather conditions to stay behind?
questions.explanation: The hypocrites made an excuse of extreme weather conditions to stay behind during Ghazwa Tabuk. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa tabuk.

questions.text: In the Battle of Uhud, after whose martyrdom did Hazrat Ali (R.A) take up the standard?
questions.explanation: In the Battle of Uhud, Hazrat Ali (R.A) took up the standard after the martyrdom of Hazrat Musab bin Umair (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Near which city is the site of Ohad located?
questions.explanation: The site of Ohad (Uhud) is located near Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud.

questions.text: In which year was the Battle of Uhud fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Uhud was fought in 625 AD (3 AH) between the Muslims of Madina and the Quraysh of Makkah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud.

questions.text: Which Sahabi is known to be buried at the site of the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Hamza (RA), the beloved uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) and the "Lion of Allah," is buried at the site of the Battle of Uhud along with other martyrs. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud.

questions.text: Who was responsible for the martyrdom of Hazrat Hamza (RA) during the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred by Wahshi bin Harb, an Abyssinian slave, during the Battle of Uhud. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud.

questions.text: Who was the leader of the Quraysh during the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: The leader of the Quraysh during the Battle of Uhud was Abu Sufyan. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud.

questions.text: How many skillful archers did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) select to stay on the mountain during the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) selected 50 skillful archers to stay on the mountain (Jabal al-Rumah) during the Battle of Uhud. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ghazwa uhud.

questions.text: What is the term for the dowry amount that is paid immediately after the nikkah in an Islamic marriage?
questions.explanation: The dowry amount paid immediately after the nikkah is called Mahr al-Muajjal. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic terminology key concepts (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which month is the fifth month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The fifth month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar is Jumada al-Awwal. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic terminology key concepts.

questions.text: In which year did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) send letters to various kings inviting them to Islam?
questions.explanation: Note: the letters to rulers were sent at the end of 6 AH / start of 7 AH, after Hudaybiyyah. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent letters to various kings inviting them to Islam in the year 6 AH, following the Treaty of Hudaibia. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who was the ruler of the Byzantine Empire to whom the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent a letter?
questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent a letter to Heraclius, the Byzantine Emperor, inviting him to Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: Which ruler sent a white mule named 'Duldul' as a gift to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The white mule named 'Duldul' was sent as a gift to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) by Maqauqis of Egypt. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: Who was appointed by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as his envoy to the King of Abyssinia?
questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) appointed Amr ibn Umayyah as his envoy to the Negus (King) of Abyssinia. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: What was the reaction of Khosrow II, the Emperor of Iran, upon receiving the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) letter?

options.B: He tore the letter into pieces

questions.explanation: Khosrow II (Parvez), the Emperor of Iran, tore the letter into pieces upon receiving the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) invitation to Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: During which years did Heraclius rule the Byzantine Empire?
questions.explanation: Heraclius ruled the Byzantine Empire from 610 to 641 A.D. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: Which companion of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was sent as an ambassador to the Roman Emperor?
questions.explanation: The companion sent as an ambassador to the Roman Emperor Heraclius was Hazrat Dihyah bin Khalifa Kalbi (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: Which ruler of Egypt did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) send a letter to after the Treaty of Hudaibia?
questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent a letter to Maqauqas, the ruler of Egypt, inviting him to Islam after the Treaty of Hudaibia. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, letters to kings.

questions.text: In which year did the significant event of Shab-e-Miraj occur in the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The event of Shab-e-Miraj (the Night Journey and Ascension) occurred in 621 A.D, approximately one year before the Hijrah to Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: During the Night Journey (Miraj), which Prophet did Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) meet at the first heaven?
questions.explanation: At the first heaven during Miraj, Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) met Hazrat Adam (AS). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: During the event of Meraj, on which heaven did Hazrat Musa (A.S) meet the Holy Prophet ﷺ?
questions.explanation: During Meraj, the Holy Prophet ﷺ met Hazrat Musa (A.S) on the 6th Heaven. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: On which level of heaven did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet Prophet Idris (A.S) during the event of Mi'raj?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ met Prophet Idris (A.S) on the 4th level of heaven during the event of Mi'raj. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: Which structure is located directly above the Kaaba and is circumambulated by seventy thousand angels daily?
questions.explanation: Bait al-Mamur is the heavenly structure located directly above the Kaaba in the seventh sky, circumambulated by seventy thousand angels daily. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: On which heaven did Hazrat Yahya (A.S) meet the Holy Prophet ﷺ during the journey of Meraj?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Yahya (A.S) met the Holy Prophet ﷺ on the 2nd Heaven during the journey of Meraj. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: On which date is Shab-e-Mairaj observed in the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: Note: 27 Rajab is the traditional date; the exact date of Miraj is disputed among scholars. Shab-e-Mairaj is observed on the 27th Rajab in the Islamic calendar. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, meraj.

questions.text: When did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) purchase the camel named Qaswa?

options.A: At the time of the Farewell Pilgrimage

questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) purchased the camel named Qaswa during the Hijrah to Madinah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migration to madina (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which tribe did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) perform his first Friday prayer (Jummah)?
questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) performed his first Friday prayer (Jummah) among the tribe of Banu Salim during the migration to Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migration to madina (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) offer the first Jumma prayer after migration to Madina?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) offered the first Jumma prayer in 1 A.H after migration to Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migration to madina.

questions.text: Where is the historical graveyard of Jannat-ul-Baqi located?
questions.explanation: The historical graveyard of Jannat-ul-Baqi is located in Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migration to madina.

questions.text: Where did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) establish his court after the migration to Madina?
questions.explanation: After migrating to Madina, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) established his court and administrative center at Masjid-e-Nabvi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migration to madina.

questions.text: Which companion of the Holy Prophet (SAAW) recited verses of the Holy Quran in the presence of Najjashi?
questions.explanation: The companion who recited verses of the Holy Quran in the presence of Najjashi was Hazrat Jaffar Tyar (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which Nabvi year did the first migration to Habsha (Abyssinia) take place?
questions.explanation: Fixed: the first migration to Abyssinia took place in Rajab of the 5th year of Prophethood (615 AD). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha.

questions.text: Which relatives of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) participated in the first migration to Abyssinia?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's (PBUH) son-in-law Usman (R.A) and his daughter Ruqayya (R.A) were the relatives who participated in the first migration to Abyssinia. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha.

questions.text: In which Islamic month did the emigrants return from Abyssinia (Habsha)?
questions.explanation: Low confidence: the migrants are reported to have returned in Shawwal of the 5th Nabawi year. The emigrants returned from Abyssinia (Habsha) in the Islamic month of Shawwal. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha.

questions.text: Which ruler's funeral was conducted by the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) despite being far from Madina?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) performed the funeral prayer (Salat-ul-Ghaib) of Negus of Habsha (Najashi) despite being far from Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha.

questions.text: How many women accompanied the second migration to Abyssinia?
questions.explanation: The second migration to Abyssinia (Habsha) included 18 women among the emigrants. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha.

questions.text: How did King Najashi react after listening to the passage from Surah Maryam?

options.A: He rejected the message and asked the Muslims to leave
options.B: He wept and acknowledged the common source of the passage and the Anjeel
options.C: He remained silent and referred the matter to his bishops
options.D: He accepted Islam immediately and abdicated his throne

questions.explanation: King Najashi wept and acknowledged the common source of the passage and the Anjeel after listening to the verses from Surah Maryam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, migrations to habsha.

questions.text: The Battle of Sariya is known as a battle in which _?

options.B: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) led the army himself

questions.explanation: The Battle of Sariya is known as a battle in which Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) did not participate. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous ghazwat expeditions (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which year did the Ghazwa of Banu Nadhir take place during the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The Ghazwa of Banu Nadhir took place in 4 A.H (Rabi' al-Awwal) during the Islamic calendar. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous ghazwat expeditions.

questions.text: During which Ghazwa was the revelation of Tayammum granted to the Muslims?
questions.explanation: The revelation of Tayammum (dry ablution) was granted to the Muslims during Ghazwa Banu Mustaliq. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous ghazwat expeditions.

questions.text: Who led the last Sariya (military expedition) during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: Fixed: the last expedition dispatched by the Prophet (PBUH) was the army of Usama bin Zaid (RA) towards Syria; it set out after his passing under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous ghazwat expeditions.

questions.text: Which mosque was ordered by Allah to be destroyed?
questions.explanation: The mosque ordered by Allah to be destroyed was Masjid Zirar, built by hypocrites to cause disunity among Muslims. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah madinan period (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which city was the Masjid e Zarar located during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H)?
questions.explanation: Masjid e Zarar was located in Madina during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah madinan period.

questions.text: Who were responsible for the construction of the Mosque Zarrar according to Islamic history?
questions.explanation: Masjid-e-Zarrar was built by the Hypocrites (Munafiqeen) of Madina under the leadership of Abu Amir to harm the Muslim community. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah madinan period.

questions.text: Where was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) laid to rest after his passing?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was laid to rest in Madina, in the chamber of his wife Aisha (R.A), which is now part of Masjid-e-Nabawi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah madinan period.

questions.text: Who is the Christian-turned-Muslim writer of the biography Muhammad: His Life Based on the Earliest Sources?
questions.explanation: The Christian-turned-Muslim writer of the biography *Muhammad: His Life Based on the Earliest Sources* is Martin Lings (also known as Abu Bakr Siraj ad-Din). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah makkan period (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What is the central theme of the book 'Zad al-Ma'ad fi Huda Khayr al-Ibad'?
questions.explanation: The central theme of 'Zad al-Ma'ad fi Huda Khayr al-Ibad' is Seerah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah makkan period.

questions.text: Where is Jannat al-Mu'alla located?
questions.explanation: Jannat al-Mu'alla is located in Mecca. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah makkan period (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who wrote an 'Essay on life of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)'?
questions.explanation: Fixed: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote "A Series of Essays on the Life of Mohammed" (1870) in reply to William Muir. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah makkan period.

questions.text: Who wrote the first book on Seerah Rasool Ullah?
questions.explanation: Fixed: Muhammad ibn Ishaq (d. 150/151 AH) wrote the first comprehensive Seerah; Ibn Hisham later edited/abridged it. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah makkan period.

questions.text: What is the name of the famous book written by Ibn Hisham?
questions.explanation: Ibn Hisham's famous book is Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, which is an edited and abridged version of Ibn Ishaq's earlier biography of the Prophet (PBUH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous seerah makkan period.

questions.text: Which month is the seventh month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.explanation: The seventh month of the Islamic calendar is Rajab. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: According to Islamic tradition, what was the first creation of Allah?
questions.explanation: According to Islamic tradition, the first creation of Allah was the Pen (Qalam). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous.

questions.text: How many obligatory acts (Faraid) are there in Ghusl (ritual purification bath) according to Islamic teachings?
questions.explanation: There are 3 obligatory acts (Faraid) in Ghusl according to Islamic teachings. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous.

questions.text: Which is the first mosque ever built on Earth according to Islamic tradition?
questions.explanation: According to Islamic tradition, Masjid-ul-Haram (Bait-ul-Allah) in Makkah is the first mosque ever built on Earth. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous.

questions.text: Which angel is responsible for taking the souls of living beings according to Islamic belief?
questions.explanation: The angel responsible for taking the souls of living beings is Hazrat Izraeel (AS), also known as Malak-ul-Maut (the Angel of Death). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous.

questions.text: Which angel is responsible for the provision of rain and food according to Islamic belief?
questions.explanation: The angel responsible for the provision of rain and food (sustenance) according to Islamic belief is Hazrat Meekail (Michael) A.S. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous.

questions.text: Which person is known as the 'Teacher of Madina'?
questions.explanation: The person known as the 'Teacher of Madina' is Musab Bin Umair (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What is meant by the term 'Mithaq' in Islamic history?
questions.explanation: The term 'Mithaq' in Islamic history means Covenant, referring to a solemn pledge or agreement. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: Which two tribes in Madina accepted Islam at the time of the Prophet Muhammad's migration (Hijrah)?
questions.explanation: The two tribes in Madina that accepted Islam at the time of the Prophet's migration were Ows and Khazraj. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: Who was sent by the Prophet to Yasrib to teach the Qur'an and Islam after the First Pledge of Aqba?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Musab bin Umair (RA) to Yasrib after the First Pledge of Aqba to teach the Qur'an and Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: How many people from Yasrib participated in the First Pledge of Aqba in 621 A.D.?
questions.explanation: 12 people from Yathrib participated in the First Pledge of Aqabah in 621 A.D. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the first ambassador of Islam by the Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H)?
questions.explanation: The first ambassador of Islam appointed by the Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was Hazrat Mus'ab bin Umair (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: In which year did a deputation from Madina accept Islam?
questions.explanation: A deputation from Madina accepted Islam in the year 620 A.D. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: How many people, including men and women, participated in the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
questions.explanation: The Second Pledge of Aqabah was attended by 73 men and 2 women. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, pledges of aqabah.

questions.text: Who among the following was the slave of Hazrat Khadija before marrying the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The slave of Hazrat Khadija (R.A) before her marriage to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was Mysra. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, servants belongings.

questions.text: What material was used to craft the seal of the Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H)?
questions.explanation: The seal of the Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was crafted from silver. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, servants belongings.

questions.text: The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed to last for how many years?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed to last for 10 years. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: During the Treaty of Hudaibia, which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) was detained by the Quraysh?
questions.explanation: The companion detained by the Quraysh during the Treaty of Hudaibia was Hazrat Usman (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia.

questions.text: How many companions of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) were present at the Bait-e-Shajrah?
questions.explanation: The number of companions of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) present at Bait-e-Shajrah was 1400. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia.

questions.text: According to the Treaty of Hudaibia, in what condition were Muslims required to carry their swords in the following year?

options.A: Not allowed to carry swords at all

questions.explanation: According to the Treaty of Hudaibia, Muslims were required to carry their swords sheathed when they returned for Umrah the following year. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia.

questions.text: What rumor spread among Muslims when Hazrat Usman (R.A) stayed longer in Makkah during his mission to negotiate with the Quraysh?

options.B: He was martyred by the Quraysh
options.D: He was taken as a prisoner of war

questions.explanation: When Hazrat Usman (R.A) was delayed in Makkah during negotiations, a rumor spread that he was martyred by the Quraysh, which led to the Pledge of Ridwan (Bait-e-Ridwan) under the tree. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia.

questions.text: Who served as the representative of the Quraish during the Treaty of Hudaibiya negotiations?
questions.explanation: The Quraish appointed Sohail bin Umro as their representative to negotiate the Treaty of Hudaibiya with the Prophet (PBUH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia.

questions.text: Which two parties signed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?

options.A: Makkan tribe of Quraysh and the Muslims
options.B: Makkan tribe of Quraysh and the Jews of Madina
options.C: Muslims and the tribe of Banu Bakr

questions.explanation: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed between the Makkan tribe of Quraysh and the Muslims in 6 AH (628 CE). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, treaty of hudaibia.

questions.text: In which year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declare the Year of Sorrow?
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared the Year of Sorrow in 619 AD. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, year of sorrow (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: After the Year of Sorrow, where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) go to preach Islam?
questions.explanation: After the Year of Sorrow, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) went to Taif to preach Islam, where he was harshly rejected and pelted with stones. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, year of sorrow.

questions.text: In which year did Hazrat Khadija (RA), the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), pass away?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Khadija (RA) passed away in 619 A.D, a year famously known as the Year of Sorrow (Aam-ul-Huzn). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, year of sorrow.
